result:
I’d make the reality of other minds impossible to ignore—not as a moral rule, but as a basic perceptual fact. You’d look at another person and feel, as directly as you feel your own hunger, that they are as real to themselves as you are to yourself.

Most cruelty needs some layer of abstraction: “they’re not like us,” “they’re a number,” “they don’t really count.” Remove that blindness and the world doesn’t become perfect, but it becomes much harder to organize harm. Every other problem—power, scarcity, conflict—would have to be fought on different terms.
